Theme

Latin word

fingō

fingō, fingere, fīnxī, fictum

verb, third conjugation

shape, form; make up; imagine, picture in the mind; pretend; suppose, imagine (that)

In this lexicon

  • create

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.23: fingere et cōnstruere nīdōs (Lewis & Short)

  • imagine

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Mil. 79: fingite animīs; Cic. N.D. 3.47: quae cōgitātiōne nōbīsmet ipsīs possumus fingere

  • pretend

    the recommended word · classical

  • suppose

    also used · classical · Cic. Ac. 2.117: finge aliquem nunc fierī sapientem, nōndum esse; Quint. 1.1.24: fingāmus igitur Alexandrum darī nōbīs

Examples

  • fingite animīs — līberae sunt enim nostrae cōgitātiōnēs et quae volunt sīc intuentur ut ea cernimus quae vidēmus

    picture it in your minds — for our thoughts are free, and they see what they wish as plainly as we see what is before our eyesCic. Mil. 79

    In the entry for imagine

  • recordāre igitur illum, M. Antōnī, diem quō dictātūram sustulistī; pōne ante oculōs laetitiam senātūs populīque Rōmānī

    remember, then, Mark Antony, the day on which you abolished the dictatorship; picture the joy of the senate and the Roman peopleCic. Phil. 2.115

    In the entry for imagine

  • Fingāmus tē esse coquum.

    Let’s pretend you’re the cook.composed

    I’ll pretend I’m just going out.Ter. Eun. 3.2.8 (Lewis & Short s.v. quasi)
